intro.title: Your first C# program
bullets: C# runs on the .NET platform
Every program starts at the Main() method
Console.WriteLine() prints a line to the screen
Every statement ends with a semicolon ;
narration: C# is built for the .NET platform. That's the runtime that actually runs your code.
Every program needs a starting point. In C#, that's the Main() method.
Want to print something to the screen? Console.WriteLine() is your go-to.
And don't forget the semicolon. It tells the compiler where one statement ends.

chatGreeting: Welcome to the start of your journey with C# basics.
I'm Leo. Let's set up your tools and get comfortable with the essentials.
If you have any questions along the way, just give me a shout.

q1.a: Main() is where your program starts running. Think of it as the front door of a house: when you hit Run, .NET finds Main() and executes it line by line.

q2.q: Why do lines end with a semicolon?
q2.a: The ; tells the compiler a statement is finished, like a full stop at the end of a sentence. Leave one out and the compiler gets confused right away. Try removing one in the hands-on task!

q3.a: Put a $ before the string, then drop variables inside {curly braces}. For example, $"Hello, {role}!" prints the value of role. Much tidier than gluing strings together with +!
